tldr: A public proposal cap creates an exact calibration boundary in a fixed four-geography switchback experiment. Finite-record inference holds on a bounded finite-table class with a constant four-unit average effect and a fixed positive floor for all three partition baseline variances; no interpolation or smoothness is needed. Individual effects and baselines may vary arbitrarily over periods within those restrictions. The sharp uniform boundary for deterministic-variance Gaussian calibration is \(T(2/3)^{m_T}\to\infty\). At every cap, the observed period-contrast variance instead gives an actual-record studentized Gaussian limit and connected 90 percent intervals with a universal \(O(T^{-1/2})\) coverage error. The original bounded \(C^1\) subclass remains the setting for explicit occupation-path limits, critical two-state variance laws, the two cancellation mechanisms, and the completed certified critical-mixture evaluator. The maintained average-effect and partition-floor restrictions are substantive conditions on unknown fixed tables. The separating witness transfers the cap obstruction to any published-model subclass containing it; no full-anchor sufficiency is asserted.
gap: Sequentially rerandomized switchback inference assumes concentration of its predictable bracket. Existing generic mixture theory leaves the variance law to be supplied, and existing best-choice budget theory studies a growing unit population with one final allocation. Zeng et al. (2026), Section 3.2.1, uses a constant additive sharp null across every unit and period for randomization inference; it does not establish the present constant four-unit average restriction as a standard condition. Positive finite-population variance alone does not impose the simultaneous partitionwise separation maintained here.
fill: Exact algorithmic reduction, original-time occupation coupling, an iff calibration frontier and observed-record variance recovery form one narrow technical contribution on the eligible class. The maintained constant four-unit average effect, together with the public randomizer's independent orientations, yields the centered-record sign factorization; it permits individual heterogeneity and time variation and does not identify the full potential table. The legal separating and equal-integral crossing tables attain minimum squared contrast \(1/16\), above the fixed floor, demonstrating nonvacuity with constant and time-varying baselines. Uniform observed-record studentization covers every public integer cap on that full class. A certified numerical construction supplies the remaining distributional evaluation obligation.
